Defining Ordered Logistic Distribution

```{julia}
struct OrderedLogistic{T1,T2} <: DiscreteUnivariateDistribution
    ŋ::T1
    cutpoints::Vector{T2}
end

function Distributions.logpdf(d::OrderedLogistic, k::Int)
    Κ = length(d.cutpoints) + 1
    c = d.cutpoints

    if k == 1
        logp = log(logistic(c[k] - d.ŋ))
    elseif k < Κ
        logp = log(logistic(c[k] - d.ŋ) - logistic(c[k-1] - d.ŋ))
    else
        logp = log(1 - logistic(c[k-1] - d.ŋ))
    end
end
```

```{julia}
# Turing model

@model m(X, y) = begin
    D = size(X, 2)

    # priors
    σ ~ Truncated(Normal(0, 1), 0, Inf)

    c1 ~ Normal(0, 20)

    log_diff_c ~ Normal(0, 2)
    c2 = c1 + exp(log_diff_c)
    c = [c1, c2]

    β ~ MvNormal(zeros(D), σ * ones(D))

    lp = X * β

    # likelihood
    for i = 1:length(y)
        y[i] ~ OrderedLogistic(lp[i], c)
    end
end
```

```{julia}
steps = 10_000
chain = sample(m(X, y), NUTS(steps, 0.65));


show(chain)
```
